The Corocoro grunt Orthopristis rubra is a haemulid fish inhabiting coastal waters of the tropical eastern Pacific, where its demersal, adhesive eggs are deposited over structured reef habitat following a broadcast spawning event. This minute initial mass places the species among the smaller offspring producers within Haemulidae, a pattern consistent with the energetic constraints of producing large numbers of small, pelagic larvae that must locate suitable settlement habitat. This extended lifespan is notable for a fish of this body size and aligns with the life-history pattern of slow-growing, iteroparous teleosts in stable tropical environments. The reproductive schedule inferred from otolith microchemistry and trap-catch data suggests that females produce approximately 822 eggs per day [Ri = approximately 822 eggs per day] during the peak spawning season when water temperatures approach 25.7 °C [T = 25.7 °C].
